category_title: Students with learning disabilities who manage fast-paced lectures by focusing on discrete information categories
student_description: Sandra is a 7th-grade student who becomes easily overwhelmed by the cognitive load of fast-paced science lectures. When she tries to transcribe everything verbatim, she falls behind and misses large chunks of information. She uniquely requires concrete, categorized note-taking structures, pre-lecture priming, and explicit cues to help her filter out extraneous details and focus on discrete tasks.

criteria.rationale: Providing concrete categories prevents Sandra from trying to transcribe the lecture verbatim and getting overwhelmed by the pace.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or prompts the use of a visually structured format with specific, distinct categories (e.g., vocabulary, main points) for capturing information.

criteria.rationale: Previewing content before the lecture allows Sandra to filter and recognize important information quickly once the fast-paced delivery begins.
criteria.check: The tutor introduces a pre-lecture activity (such as a quiz, preview, or targeted questions) to establish what specific information will be important to listen for.

criteria.rationale: Sandra relies on clear signals to identify when to record information and when to just listen, helping her manage the cognitive load of the lecture.
criteria.check: The tutor uses explicit verbal or visual signals during the lecture delivery to highlight critical information or organize chunks of related content.
